title: Imaging machines measured before and after

blocks.text: A hospital group replaces imaging machines. For each candidate the clinical engineers record three measures with the old machine (`before`) and with its replacement (`after`): hours of downtime a year and energy used, where lower is better, and scans a day, where higher is better (`HIGHER_IS_BETTER` says which is which). Each measure has a reference (the swing the board agreed on, in the measure's own unit) and a weight.

Write `improvement(measure, before, after)`, how much better a measure gets, so that more is always better, and `project_score(project, reference, weights)`, the weighted sum of each improvement as a share of its reference. `plan_score` (given) adds the scores of the projects a plan funds; the tests call both.

The board will compare plans of different sizes by their total score, so be careful what a score of 0 means. A replacement that makes one measure worse (a new machine that uses more energy) should lose score for it, and the loss is not capped. About four lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from imaging import Replacement, plan_score, project_score

reference = {"downtime_hours": 50, "scans_per_day": 20, "energy_mwh": 200}
weights = {"downtime_hours": 0.4, "scans_per_day": 0.4, "energy_mwh": 0.2}
projects = {
    "Mammo": Replacement("Mammo", {"downtime_hours": 60, "scans_per_day": 30, "energy_mwh": 90},
                         {"downtime_hours": 35, "scans_per_day": 40, "energy_mwh": 70}),
    "Fluoro": Replacement("Fluoro", {"downtime_hours": 30, "scans_per_day": 15, "energy_mwh": 100},
                          {"downtime_hours": 20, "scans_per_day": 15, "energy_mwh": 140}),
}

for name, p in projects.items():
    print(f"{name} score:", round(project_score(p, reference, weights), 4))
print("plan Mammo + Fluoro:", round(plan_score(["Mammo", "Fluoro"], projects, reference, weights), 4))
print("empty plan:", plan_score([], projects, reference, weights))

cases.says: a project's score is its normalized, weighted improvements, worked out by hand, with lower-is-better measures counted by their fall
adding a project that changes no measure leaves the plan's score where it was
a measure that gets worse lowers the project's score rather than counting as zero
a plan scores the sum of its projects' scores, not their average, and an empty plan scores 0

origin.section: Zero Must Mean No Benefit When Scores Are Added Across Projects

concepts: a score summed over the projects of a plan needs its zero at no benefit
